Owner Takes His Chevy Corvette to a Tuner, Goes Home With 800 Horsepower
11 photos
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube
A bodyguard from New Jersey bought a C7 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 out of North Carolina, but he knew he wanted more even before he wired the money. So he sent it straight to a tuner in Houston, Texas, and asked the experts to ship it to his home in New Jersey once they were done. A couple of weeks later, he got exactly what he wanted.
Sometimes, just sometimes, what sports cars can do is not enough for the owners. Some ship it to tuners with only delivery mileage on the clock. Others drive it to shops to get them upgraded after years of dealing with the stock performance. And others, like Dave from New Jersey, buy a pre-owned car and, even before driving it home, send it straight to a tuner.
This is exactly what Dave from New Jersey did. When it rolled off the production line of the General Motors Bowling Green Assembly Plant in Bowling Green, Kentucky, the previous-gen Corvette Z06 was powered by the 6.2-liter supercharged LT4 V8, pushing out 650 horsepower (659 metric horsepower) and 650 pound-feet (881 Newton meters) of torque.
Those were enough to make the car rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in just 2.95 seconds, run the quarter mile in 10.95 seconds with a trap speed of 127 mph (204 kph) when equipped with the quickest-shifting transmission, the automatic, and max out at 185 mph (298 kph).
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube By the time he showed up, it was already decided. His car would get the LMR 800 Horsepower Package. Dave, the owner, is a bodyguard. When he brought his car in, he asked the tuners to make it faster and louder while keeping it reliable.
So, the experts came up with a cold-air intake, cam kit, upgraded pulleys, new spark plugs, American Racing headers, and an upgraded exhaust to give the C7 Chevy Corvette Z06 the boost in power, sound, and attitude. That is what the owner wanted. They also installed an upgraded expansion tank for an extra 3 gallons of coolant, and an intercooler to keep temperature under control.
The owner also asked for the lid, valve covers, and brake calipers to be powder-coated blue to match the Admiral Blue paint of the car. When he pops the hood at car shows, he will definitely steal the show. However, his Corvette Z06 is not all show and no go.
Now, Steven Fereday takes the car out for a spin to make sure that he hands over a solid build that remains reliable pull after pull. He wants to see how it shifts and how it behaves when he pushes the pedal to the metal in real driving conditions.
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube The car shifts right and sounds right, but a pair of Toyos on the rear axle would give the driver more confidence on hard pulls with traction control off.
